title: Lesson 17 - The Agentforce Data Library: A Retrieval Layer, Not a Knowledge Base
description: Explain the considerations of Agentforce Data Library and its concepts.

questions.question: What separates an Agentforce Data Library from a Salesforce Knowledge base?
options: A data library only indexes published Knowledge articles.
A data library wraps sources such as Knowledge, uploaded files, web sources and custom retrievers into searchable chunks.
A data library replaces Data 360 and needs no indexing.
A data library stores documents inside the agent's prompt template.
questions.explanation: A library is a broader retrieval layer that can index content beyond Knowledge articles, while the other options misdescribe either its sources or its dependency on Data 360.

questions.question: Before you can create an Agentforce Data Library in an org, what must be true?
options: Knowledge must be enabled and no other product is needed.
Prompt Builder must be licensed and Data 360 is optional.
A vector database must be provisioned by the customer outside Data 360.
Data 360 must be set up and activated, because every library builds objects inside it.
questions.explanation: Every library provisions a data stream, search index and retriever inside Data 360, and libraries consume Data 360 credits, so Data 360 is a prerequisite.

questions.question: An agent must answer from a specific retriever you configured in Data 360 rather than the auto-built one. What do you use?
options: A custom retriever referenced by your own prompt template.
The Answer Questions with Knowledge action with no retriever input.
A web search data library, which is read-only.
A Knowledge data category on the source article.
questions.explanation: A custom retriever wired into your own prompt template gives control over which datasets are reached, whereas the packaged action uses the retriever Salesforce builds for the library.
